title: Sequential KV Strand Allocator and Background Rewrite Sweeper
creator: Priya Raman
description:
Problem: As continuous-batching loads increase, KV cache allocation becomes highly fragmented on GPUs leading to elevated memory overhead, tail latency variability, and occasional OOMs during long-sequence traces. Existing slab and pool allocators reduce fragmentation for steady-state access patterns but struggle with bursty, append-heavy workloads (long chat sessions, streaming generation).

Goal: Introduce a sequential 'strand' allocation layer on top of the existing slab allocator to co-locate temporally adjacent KV entries, combined with a low-priority background rewrite sweeper that performs in-place rewrite + hole stitching during idle windows. The approach trades a bounded, short-term write amplification for long-term fragmentation reduction and improved batch packing.

Design summary:
- Strand allocation: group KV items by request session / batch window into append-only 'strands' allocated from contiguous GPU pages. Strands are size-bounded (configurable: 64KB–2MB) to avoid large-block waste.
- Hot-cold tagging: lightweight hotness estimate per strand based on recent hit rate and access recency; hot strands are pinned to fast lanes and excluded from aggressive rewriting.
- Background rewrite sweeper: incremental, rate-limited pass that rewrites partially-empty strands into compact destinations and frees source pages; operates only when GPU utilization < threshold and under a service-level cap to avoid impact on latency SLOs.
- Live hole stitching: when rewriting neighboring strands, perform adjacent hole coalescing to create larger free runs for future large-strand allocations, improving packing for streaming batches.
- Continuous-batching integration: allocator exposes strand affinity hints to batcher to prefer assembling batches from entries on the same strand to reduce KV lookups crossing pages and improve locality.

Telemetry & safety:
- Per-strand metrics: occupancy, hit-rate, last-access, pinned/unpinned, rewrite attempts, rewrite latency.
- Circuit breaker: if background rewrite increases p50 token latency by >5% or increases p99 by >2% for 3 consecutive windows, pause sweeper and rollback last rewrite window.
- Canary rollout: start on a subset of customers (low-traffic) then ramp.

Trade-offs considered:
- Write amplification vs fragmentation: sweeper rewrites entries (extra copies) but reduces long-term memory and coalesces holes; measured break-even at ~3% rewrite rate for typical chat workloads.
- Dedicated contiguous allocation vs flexibility: strand boundaries may increase initial internal fragmentation for small transient entries — mitigated by small minimum strand sizes and opportunistic packing of short-lived sessions into shared micro-strands.
- Complexity: additional metadata per strand (O(#strands)) increases memory accounting; we keep metadata compact (32 bytes/strand) and evict stale strands from control-plane maps when empty longer than TTL.

Deliverables:
- Strand allocator implementation in runtime (C++): allocation/deallocation, hot-cold tagging, affinity hints API.
- Background rewrite sweeper: scheduler, rewrite worker, safety circuit.
- Batcher changes: affinity-aware packing heuristics.
- End-to-end benchmarks and a perf dashboard tile.
acceptance_criteria: Fragmentation (measured as % free small slots scattered) reduced by >=40% on synthetic long-chat workload compared to baseline
Aggregate GPU memory used for KV cache reduced by >=12% at 95th percentile traffic compared to baseline
No regressions: p50 token latency change <= 3% and p99 <= 5% under load tests with sweeper enabled
Background sweeper respects circuit breaker: resumes/pauses with clear telemetry visible in Console
Canary rollout plan and automated rollback path documented and validated
Integration tests covering allocation, rewrite, hole stitching, and batcher affinity added to CI

comments: 2026-03-02 Priya Raman: Spiked a micro-prototype for contiguous strand allocation; initial results show 25% fewer page splits on sample trace (not yet accounting for rewrite overhead). Added a simple strawman for hot-cold tagging.

2026-03-04 Ethan Morales: Implemented basic allocator API (alloc/free/iterate). Pushed branch feat/strand-alloc. Unit tests added. Observed increased metadata memory by ~0.7% for 1M strands — within budget.

2026-03-06 Maya Patel (Perf): Ran long-chat workload. Fragmentation down 18% w/ no sweeper. Sweep prototype currently causes 6% p50 increase when unconstrained; added rate limiter and lowered worker concurrency — results improved.

2026-03-08 Code review by Arjun Singh: requested explicit circuit-breaker thresholds and thorough tests around concurrent rewrite+read. Also suggested avoiding full-strand rewrite when <25% reclaimable to reduce write amplification. Added follow-up task.

2026-03-10 Security review note (Zoe Kim): KMS metadata access not affected but highlighted need to ensure sweeper doesn't leak pointer-style addresses in logs. Adding redaction step to sweeper logging.

2026-03-12 Ethan Morales: Opened PR #1357 (github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/1357). CI green for unit tests; integration tests flaky in one runner due to timing — investigating. Preparing canary runbook.
2026-03-12 Priya Raman: Performance dashboard tile prototype available at https://observability.redwood.internal/dashboards/kv-strand-1357 (canary-only). Added synthetic traces to benchmark harness.
